start_here: Say to your AI: "Check these citations against their repositories: trillion-workshop/tools/git-changes/show/mount-git-worktree.tsx:21@434ee11fd0 with the quote mountReactSurface." It answers ok true, or ok false with why it was refused, for each citation.
no_lists_because: It keeps no list of its own: it reads the repositories named in citation-resolvers.json through git on this computer and answers each citation in the run.
instructions: 1. Give the citations as the input: {"items": [{"cite": "trillion-workshop/tools/git-changes/show/mount-git-worktree.tsx:21@434ee11fd0", "quote": "mountReactSurface"}]}, one item per citation. A citation is root/path:line, root/path:line-line for a range, and @commit to read the file as that commit holds it.
2. Run tool:resolve-citations with that input on this computer. It answers {"result": [{"cite", "ok", "why", "against"}]}, one verdict per citation.

3. Read each verdict: ok true means the cited line or range holds the quote at the commit named (or at the root's current ref when it names none); ok false gives why; ok null means a repository is not on this computer, so the citation was not judged.
4. Refuse any citation with ok false, and fix it with the line it names before the next step relies on it.

worked_examples.title: Check one new-home citation against the commit it names
worked_examples.expect: result[0].ok is true, against names trillion-workshop at commit 434ee11fd0
worked_examples.hands_back: result[0] says ok true for the citation, and against names trillion-workshop at commit 434ee11fd0, the commit the citation names.
